title: Monitoring & Maintaining Models 🩺
description: Detect data drift, concept drift, set up retraining pipelines, and keep your model healthy in production.

slides.title: Models Decay Over Time ⏳
slides.content:
# Why Monitoring Matters

A deployed model isn't a 'set it and forget it' artifact. Real‑world data changes, and model performance degrades.

- **Data drift**: the distribution of input features shifts (e.g., users become younger, economic indicators change).
- **Concept drift**: the relationship between features and target changes (e.g., what defines 'spam' evolves).

If you don't monitor, you'll serve increasingly bad predictions without knowing.

slides.title: Detecting Drift 🔍
slides.content:
# Statistical Tests & Metrics

- **Population Stability Index (PSI)**: measures distribution shift between reference and current data.
- **Kolmogorov‑Smirnov (KS) test**: detects if two samples come from different distributions.
- **Model performance monitoring**: track accuracy, precision, recall on ground truth labels (when available) over time.

Tools: Evidently AI, WhyLogs, NannyML, or custom pipelines.

Set up alerts when drift exceeds a threshold.

quizData.explanation: Data drift is a shift in the input data distribution, which can degrade model performance.

slides.title: Retraining Strategies 🔄
slides.content:
# Keeping the Model Fresh

- **Scheduled retraining**: retrain weekly/monthly on new data.
- **Triggered retraining**: retrain when a drift metric exceeds threshold.
- **Online learning**: update model incrementally with each new sample (e.g., SGDRegressor with `partial_fit`).

Automate the retraining pipeline (data ingestion → preprocessing → training → evaluation → deployment). This is the heart of **MLOps**.

slides.title: Simple Drift Check with PSI 🐍
slides.content: Compute PSI to compare two distributions:
slides.codeSnippet:
import numpy as np

def calculate_psi(expected, actual, buckets=10):
    breakpoints = np.linspace(0, 1, buckets+1)
    expected_percents = np.histogram(expected, bins=breakpoints)[0] / len(expected)
    actual_percents = np.histogram(actual, bins=breakpoints)[0] / len(actual)
    # avoid division by zero
    expected_percents = np.clip(expected_percents, 1e-6, 1)
    actual_percents = np.clip(actual_percents, 1e-6, 1)
    psi = np.sum((actual_percents - expected_percents) * np.log(actual_percents / expected_percents))
    return psi

quizData.question: A model that is never retrained will eventually become less accurate if the data distribution changes over time.
quizData.explanation: True. Without updates, the model's assumptions become stale, leading to decreased performance.
